$comment: S5 blind solve (methodology/05-eval-rubric.md #blind-solve). exam-examiner, fresh session, 2026-08-16. Keyless form generated by jq-stripping answer/rationale/distractor_patterns/concept metadata from questions.json; all 67 items answered with confidence + reasoning BEFORE any key was read (pre-key record preserved in session scratchpad). Encoding: single_choice chosen/keyed are option letters; multiple_response are sorted letters comma-joined; scenario_matching are 'sN=Option' pairs semicolon-joined. Result: 67/67 match, zero misses, so no adjudication entries are required (adjudication is REQUIRED only when match=false). Codex advisory cross-solve was attempted and skipped (no CLI auth in session) - see eval/codex-solve.json; per-item codex fields are therefore absent and the Gate 2 sample carries no cross-model signal. CAVEAT the examiner flags against its own 100% score: the solve was genuinely blind to the key fields, but two bank-wide surface cues (keyed option first in 67/67 items, keyed option longest in 51/57 SC items) were visible in the keyless form itself and inflate any solver's accuracy, human or model - see judge-scores.json bank_defects and derivation/eval-report.md.

items.reasoning: AI > ML > DL(neural nets); GenAI is a DL-based branch; tool-calling planner is agentic AI - only A nests the fields correctly.
Algorithm = learning procedure, model = trained artifact, nightly scoring = inference; B/C/D each break a definitional boundary.
Labeled continuous target = supervised regression; clustering ignores labels, RL has no environment, banding discards the required output.
Nightly full-manifest scoring with no daytime requests = batch inference on a managed service; always-on endpoint and self-hosting fight the workload shape.
Timestamped sensor readings = structured time-series; free-text notes = unstructured; CSV serialization does not make it tabular-in-kind.
Deterministic published-table logic (A) and negative cost-benefit (B) are the canonical when-NOT-to-use-ML findings; C is solvable via cloud, D is anecdote, E is a false claim.
Predicting a future quantity from time-ordered history is forecasting by definition; the deception framing of B is wordplay.

items.chosen: s1=Amazon Transcribe; s2=Amazon Polly; s3=Amazon Comprehend; s4=Amazon Translate; s5=Amazon Transcribe
items.keyed: s1=Amazon Transcribe; s2=Amazon Polly; s3=Amazon Comprehend; s4=Amazon Translate; s5=Amazon Transcribe
items.reasoning: Speech-to-text=Transcribe (s1,s5), TTS=Polly, NLP sentiment/key-phrase=Comprehend, language translation=Translate.
Offline flights + in-flight review + regulator explainability all point to a compact on-device traditional model; every FM option violates a stated constraint.
EDA -> pre-process -> feature engineering -> train/tune -> evaluate -> deploy -> monitor; D drops monitoring, C evaluates in prod, B inverts prep order.
Two engineers, six weeks, 1,200 labels = adapt an open-source pre-trained model; scratch training and delay both burn the grant window.
The failure is process, not tooling or staffing: MLOps discipline (tracking, repeatability, production readiness) survives individuals; B/C/D patch the person.
Unchanged artifact + shifted economy = data drift; durable response is monitoring feeding retraining, not threshold fiddling or restoring backups (weights do not decay).
2% base rate + 40x asymmetric miss cost = recall on the fraud class; board payoff question = ROI; accuracy misleads at this imbalance.
Context fit and billing are both token-denominated and English runs >1 token per word on average; B's 1:1 claim is false.
Chunk -> embed -> embed query -> nearest-neighbor distance is exactly how semantic retrieval works; whole-doc single vectors and max-size chunks degrade retrieval.
Rewriting instructions and worked examples is prompt engineering: input-side only, zero weight change, zero training cost; C mislabels it as context engineering.

items.chosen: s1=Transformer-based large language model; s2=Diffusion model; s3=Multi-modal model; s4=Transformer-based large language model; s5=Diffusion model
items.keyed: s1=Transformer-based large language model; s2=Diffusion model; s3=Multi-modal model; s4=Transformer-based large language model; s5=Diffusion model
items.reasoning: Text->text = LLM (s1,s4); text->image and image->image = diffusion (s2,s5); mixed image+text input = multi-modal (s3); s5 could arguably be called multi-modal but image-variant generation is diffusion's home turf.
Open-ended conversational + summarization across shifting topics is where GenAI uniquely earns its place; OCR wants fidelity not generation, churn is classical ML.
Data selection -> model selection -> pre-training -> fine-tuning -> evaluation -> deployment -> feedback loop; D truncates the loop at ship, B deletes evaluation.
6,000-in/400-out means input tokens drive cost (trim the prompt); a predictable nightly peak hitting on-demand limits is the textbook provisioned-throughput case.
The instructions are fine; what enters the call and how pieces are prioritized is failing - that is context engineering, not wording (B) or weights (C).
Acting on external systems = tool use; multi-day persistent state = memory management; window size, timeouts, and fine-tuning do not confer agency.
System patterns = decomposition into specialist agents; communication patterns = coordination/handoff between them; B confuses with horizontal scaling.
MCP is the open standard interface between assistants/agents and external tools and data, replacing per-vendor glue; it is not scheduling, prompting, or transport encryption.
Confident fluent fabrication is hallucination, an inherent GenAI failure mode requiring designed-in controls, not a corrupted artifact or a disclosure patch.
LLM output is nondeterministic; the design that assumed repeatability is broken - extract once, share the result; temperature 0 does not guarantee identity (C is the trap).
Hard constraints (latency, residency, cost cap) filter first, then maximize capability inside the feasible set; a leaderboard score meets none of the binding constraints.
Multi-provider FM catalog + RAG grounding + guardrails with no infra = Amazon Bedrock; SageMaker is the build-your-own path the team explicitly does not want.
Managed service = lower barrier/speed to market plus inherited security-compliance posture; C is false (no platform fixes hallucination), D describes self-hosting.
A 40k-token input several candidates cannot accept at all is a dominating hard requirement - filter on it first; parameter count and modality are not the binding constraints.
Identical 3,500-token prefix on 12k requests/day is the prompt-caching case exactly; fine-tuning rules into weights loses updatability, trimming loses fidelity.
Temperature widens sampling randomness; 1.0 left from a creativity experiment explains erratic output - lower it; no inference parameter changes model knowledge.
Knowledge newer than training data + unaffordable retraining = RAG by design; quarterly fine-tuning chases a moving target, full-library prompts blow the window.
Team runs PostgreSQL, wants that skill set: RDS for PostgreSQL with vector search (pgvector) is the AWS-listed vector store; embedding model does not dictate the store.
Canonical cost ladder cheapest-first: in-context learning < RAG < fine-tuning < pre-training, with distillation a separate compression route, not a rung.
An agent adds multi-step orchestration of tool/API calls (book, update, notify) - action coordination, not a bigger chat model or zero oversight.
Working prompts are built from parts - context, instruction, negative prompts - and refined by experiment; repetition and recency tricks are folklore, post-hoc moderation dodges the question.

items.chosen: s1=Zero-shot prompting; s2=Few-shot prompting; s3=Chain-of-thought prompting; s4=Prompt template; s5=Zero-shot prompting
items.keyed: s1=Zero-shot prompting; s2=Few-shot prompting; s3=Chain-of-thought prompting; s4=Prompt template; s5=Zero-shot prompting
items.reasoning: No examples = zero-shot (s1,s5); worked examples = few-shot; reason-step-by-step = CoT; centrally stored placeholders = template.
Planting content that gets ingested into the retrieval corpus is poisoning (corrupting data the system depends on); hijacking would be seizing the assistant's task at runtime.
Untracked console edits with no diff or rollback = missing prompt versioning; manage prompts as versioned artifacts (Bedrock Prompt Management); B/C/D are process band-aids.

Large unlabeled domain corpus + goal of terminology command across tasks = continuous pre-training; fine-tuning needs labels, scratch pre-training is unaffordable overkill, distillation is for the later kiosk variant.
Instruction-response pairs across task types = instruction tuning; specializing to field language = domain adaptation; reusing a related-task model = transfer learning.
Fine-tuning data must be labeled (signal) and representative of production traffic; max volume, strict recency, and raw authenticity are each anti-patterns.
Pairwise human preference rankings with no gold answer is precisely RLHF's data shape; SFT needs labeled correct responses the team lacks.
Subjective quality at scale = human-in-the-loop sample to set the bar, then calibrated LLM-as-judge for volume - the Bedrock Model Evaluation pairing; benchmarks do not measure persuasiveness.
ROUGE is the summarization overlap metric (BLEU is translation-oriented), and no overlap metric certifies factual correctness - the second half of the ask.
Strong component benchmarks with wrong end-to-end answers is the compose-fallacy lesson: evaluate the application on real questions; B/C guess at causes, D lowers the bar.
Board asks about business value: task completion rate and cost per interaction vs human baseline; ROUGE and leaderboards are model metrics, brand-survey attribution is noise.
Fairness/inclusivity from data = diverse curated sources spanning served populations + balanced classes/groups; volume alone (C) and single-market uniformity (D) are anti-answers.
Topic blocking + content/PII filtering on prompts and responses without retraining = Bedrock Guardrails at the interaction boundary; system-prompt pleading is not enforcement.
Both models meet the accuracy target, so the training/inference energy difference is a legitimate responsible-AI selection criterion tipping to mid-size; B/C/D each dismiss or offset it.
Generative-specific register entries: IP infringement from generated content and biased outputs, both feeding end-user risk and trust loss; B/C ignore the generative capability, D is concealment.
99% train vs 71% validation/live = overfitting (memorization), with concentrated misses showing the fit failure landing unevenly on one product line; underfitting would depress both scores.
Bias is found by subgroup performance analysis, label-quality review, and human audits (A2I for structured review); aggregate accuracy on fresh data (B) is exactly what hides subgroup harm.
Transparency = what the system is and how built; explainability = why a particular output; the regulator asked for one of each, so one document conflating them fails both.
Explainability reaching people = Model Cards (purpose/limits), Clarify (bias + attributions), OSS/licensing disclosure, human-centered feedback; B is security telemetry, C is PR.
Defensible high-stakes triage forces the interpretable 91% model - the canonical performance-vs-interpretability tradeoff; post-hoc explanation of the ensemble (C) is rationalization.

First control for differentiated team access across data/models/endpoints = least-privilege IAM, extended to agent actions (AgentCore Identity/Policy); prompts are not access control, CloudTrail is detection after the fact.
Protected in place and in motion = KMS encryption at rest + in transit; off the public internet = PrivateLink; reviews and notices are paperwork, broad read access is the opposite of control.
Unpredictably scattered PII in training text: discover with Macie, then privacy-enhancing tech + access control before training; Inspector scans workloads/vulnerabilities not data content.
SaaS -> platform build moves the customer up the shared-responsibility stack; the GenAI Security Scoping Matrix maps exactly this shift onto data protection, model config, and output controls.
Must never emit = output-side control set: leakage prevention, filtering/validation, toxicity, hallucination detection via grounding; input screening cannot stop model-originated leakage.
Instructions smuggled in untrusted document text that the model obeyed = prompt injection; counter is input-boundary segregation of data from instructions plus capability limits.
Know where answers came from = lineage/citation via cataloging (inbound); prove what was said = interaction audit trail (outbound); model versions alone reconstruct neither.
History of API calls with caller identity and timing = CloudTrail event history; Config tracks resource configuration, CloudWatch counts invocations without attribution.
Every finding is a lapsed obligation, not a wrong document: governance is an operated lifecycle (cadence, training, monitoring), so A names the failure; B rewrites the binder, C buys a tool.
